extracted.intended_audience: General public; hikers, zookeepers, and conservationists interested in vultures
extracted.subtask_description: Compose an informational species profile about vultures for a general audience, covering identification, habitat, diet, behavior, conservation threats, and practical advice for observers and caretakers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finding vultures in the wild
rubrics_metrics.description: How to locate and observe vultures in natural settings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look skyward for thermal soaring and groups circling on warm air currents; watch for congregations around potential food sources or perched on tall trees, cliffs, or communication towers, especially during cooler parts of the day. Examples: Turkey Vultures in forested areas (use sense of smell), large groups in open grasslands or savannas. Anti-patterns: expecting them only at ground level or in dense forest where visibility is poor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observe from a distance
rubrics_metrics.description: Guideline for hikers and casual observers to avoid disturbing vultures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain a respectful distance if you encounter a vulture, especially at a carcass; vultures are generally shy and will not pose a threat to humans. Do not approach or try to feed them. Disturbing birds at a carcass or nest can disrupt feeding and breeding behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not approach nests
rubrics_metrics.description: Protective rule to prevent disturbance of breeding vultures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you discover a nest, observe from afar and avoid disturbing the birds, particularly during breeding season. Nests are typically in elevated, secure locations (cliffs, tall trees, caves); approaching nests risks predation and nest abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dietary management for captive vultures
rubrics_metrics.description: Feeding and nutrition standards for zookeepers and caretakers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a consistent diet of fresh, high-quality carrion (thawed rodents, chicks, or larger carcasses) to mimic natural diet. Supplement vitamins and minerals as needed (especially for growing chicks or breeding adults). Avoid feeding meat treated with harmful veterinary drugs (e.g., diclofenac) that are toxic to vultures. Example guidance: match carrion type and decomposition stage to species preferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hygiene and enclosure maintenance
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for enclosure cleanliness and structural needs in captivity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enclosures require rigorous cleaning to prevent bacterial buildup; provide ample perching opportunities at varying heights and ensure access to bathing water. Rationale: vultures are naturally clean birds and hygiene reduces disease risk. Anti-patterns: overcrowded perches, poor drainage, lack of bathing opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enrichment to stimulate natural behaviors
rubrics_metrics.description: Behavioral enrichment practices to promote physical and mental health.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer varied feeding schedules, hide food, provide different textures or objects to manipulate, and create opportunities for soaring in large aviaries. Examples: providing bones for species that specialize on bone marrow (Bearded Vulture) or objects to encourage tool use (Egyptian Vulture). Avoid monotonous feeding that does not encourage foraging behaviors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Health monitoring and veterinary care
rubrics_metrics.description: Ongoing health surveillance and proactive medical care for captive vultures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct regular veterinary checks; monitor for signs of illness, changes in appetite, or behavioral abnormalities. Pay particular attention to bone health (risk of metabolic bone disease) and other species-specific issues. Promptly investigate appetite/behavior changes and establish preventive care schedules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Breeding program best practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for captive breeding and species survival programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For endangered species, participate in Species Survival Plans (SSPs) or similar programs, carefully manage genetics, and provide optimal conditions for reproduction and chick rearing. Guidance includes shared incubation duties, secure nesting sites, and long-term parental care planning. Anti-patterns: unmanaged captive breeding that ignores genetic diversity or proper husbandry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conservation measures and policy actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommended conservation strategies to halt or reverse vulture declines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key measures include banning harmful veterinary drugs (e.g., diclofenac), establishing vulture safe zones, supporting captive breeding programs (e.g., California Condor efforts), and running public awareness campaigns. Examples: drug bans, protected foraging/nesting habitat, targeted education to reduce persecution. Scoring note: prioritize actions addressing the single greatest threat (poisoning).

rubrics_metrics.name: Threat identification and mitigation priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Listing and prioritizing the main threats to vultures and corresponding mitigation focuses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary threats: poisoning (secondary poisoning from treated carcasses), habitat loss and degradation (urbanization, agriculture, infrastructure), food scarcity (declines in wild ungulates), electrocution and collision (power lines, wind turbines), and direct persecution driven by misinformation. Mitigation: eliminate sources of poisoning, protect/restore habitat, ensure food availability measures, retrofit dangerous infrastructure, and counter misinformation through outreach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vultures as ecosystem engineers and disease preventers
rubrics_metrics.description: Principle describing the ecological value and justification for protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vultures rapidly consume carrion, preventing proliferation of disease-carrying bacteria and viruses (e.g., botulism, cholera, anthrax) and accelerating nutrient cycling. This service is framed as critical to public and livestock health; conservation actions can be justified by ecosystem and human health benefits. Example messaging: 'Healthy vulture populations are indicators of a healthy ecosystem.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Understanding social dynamics at carcasses and roosts
rubrics_metrics.description: Behavioral criteria for interpreting vulture group behavior and hierarchy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect communal roosting, formation of feeding hierarchies where larger species feed first, and named groupings (kettle in flight, committee resting, wake feeding). Use these observations to infer species interactions and resource availability. Anti-patterns: misinterpreting congregation solely as aggressive behavior rather than information-sharing and hierarchy.
